searchText: I have to check the deposit contract but the event report `bytes` which could thus could mean the logged bytes could be of variable length. Hard-coding the index value which denotes the start of the bytes thus means that if the contract logs the event the bytes length is always of the same size 🤔 We are currently ABI-decoding it but if it is indeed fixed lenghts we can also hardcode these constant indices anyone else implement t9s? https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/tree/master/cmd/evm#transaction-tool I think to verify bounds of the 7702 txs clients will need to implement the t11s tool. It's a "transaction" checker which takes an RLP list of txs and verifies encoding / decoding integrity. e.g. to ensure that clients will reject transactions with a chain ID > 2^64, we would encode such a special tx RLP and try to decode with t11s Doesn't eest test this also? I think there are tests which are required to fail which check this the problem is filling / consuming the tests. we already fail during json deserialization. it's the same way we'd fail with block deserialization Besu only has t8n and b11r. The reasons for those are they are what the EEST loop uses. Having EEST use t9s is the best way to encourage adoption, and is similar to the EOF validation checks.
